question: Can translation symmetry in low-order word co-occurrence statistics explain why language-model representations of cyclic time, historical time, and geography form circles, rippled one-dimensional curves, and spatial manifolds, why their coordinates are linearly decodable, and why the geometry survives removal of direct target-target statistics?

method.core_idea: Approximate word-embedding learning as spectral factorization of a bounded, normalized co-occurrence matrix M*, assume that words on a latent temporal or spatial continuum have pair statistics depending only on latent distance, and diagonalize the resulting translation-invariant kernel to predict representation coordinates as Fourier modes.
method.mechanism: The authors construct M* from weighted skip-gram probabilities on a 2.72B-token November-2023 English Wikipedia corpus, then obtain spectral word embeddings by diagonalizing M*. Periodic latent lattices yield discrete sine/cosine pairs; an exponential kernel on an open interval yields centered sine/cosine modes with noninteger wavenumbers; monotonically ordered modes turn linear probing into truncated Fourier reconstruction. The predicted curves and spatial eigenmodes are compared visually with constructed word embeddings, Gemma 2 2B residual-stream activations, and 308M-parameter EmbeddingGemma vectors. A seasonal latent-variable model explains collective robustness, and target month-month entries are zeroed to test whether helper words reconstruct the circle.
assumptions: The quartic word2vec approximation and its matrix-factorization optimum faithfully represent the geometry learned by actual word2vec-like optimization.
Low-order pairwise co-occurrence structure remains a primary determinant of deep contextual transformer representations despite higher-order statistics, attention, tokenization, and prompt context.
For a semantic subset S, pair statistics depend only on Euclidean or periodic latent distance, so the relevant matrix block is translation invariant.
Calendar and historical co-occurrences are adequately modeled by periodized or open-boundary exponential kernels, respectively.
The embedding dimension is at least rank(M*) for the exact geometry theorems; lower-dimensional empirical embeddings recover the relevant top eigenspaces.
M* is positive semidefinite in the simplified theory, or the matrix absolute value |M*| has the required symmetry in the precise periodic theorem.
Eigenvalues decrease monotonically with Fourier wavenumber, allowing PCA rank to be identified with a low-pass cutoff in the coordinate-decoding theorem.
Semantic items lie on uniform lattices for the analytic results; irregular geography is expected to inherit only qualitative slow spatial modes.

The continuous latent-variable model has uniformly distributed seasonal centers, conditionally independent word occurrences, a large vocabulary, a smooth symmetric modulation kernel, and fixed embedding dimension as vocabulary size grows.
Visual mode similarity across models is sufficient evidence that the same co-occurrence mechanism generated those modes.
Removing a fixed target-target matrix block is a suitable proxy for removing direct target-target evidence from a training corpus.
PCA choices such as excluding May, omitting a tokenization-dominated Gemma component, and selecting visually convenient kernel parameters do not create the reported agreement.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported central empirical finding: calendar months and historical years follow the Fourier-like curves predicted from their measured co-occurrence kernels in spectral word embeddings and Gemma 2 2B activations.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 1 juxtaposes analytic calendar loops and open historical curves with English-Wikipedia spectral embeddings and prompted Gemma 2 2B residual activations; their centered or uncentered Gram matrices share banded temporal structure. The match is visual rather than scored, and May is excluded from the static month PCA because of polysemy.

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: exact translation symmetry on a periodic semantic lattice makes the representation PCA coordinates discrete Fourier modes.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 1 diagonalizes the centered submatrix of |M*| with lattice plane waves. Conjugate wavevectors become real sine/cosine pairs, amplitudes are square roots of the kernel's discrete Fourier coefficients, the constant mode is removed by centering, and Nyquist modes receive separate normalization. The precise result requires Assumption B.1 and embedding dimension at least rank(M*).

anchors.section: 3 Co-occurrence model with symmetry / Assumption 3.1 and Proposition 1
E.2 Proposition 1 precise statement and Equations 57-62

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: exponential distance kernels determine not just topology but the amplitudes and frequencies of calendar and historical representation manifolds.
key_findings.evidence: Corollary 2 gives integer Fourier wavenumbers for a periodized exponential kernel and amplitudes converging to sqrt(2 sigma/(1+sigma^2 k^2)). Proposition 3 handles open boundaries: odd sine and centered-even cosine modes satisfy distinct self-consistent quantization conditions and have the same spectral decay form. The proofs derive the periodic discrete transform and the open-boundary Green-function/Sturm-Liouville problem.

anchors.section: E.4 Green-function and centered eigenproblem / Equations 79-89
E.4 boundary quantization and normalization / Equations 90-98

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: under monotone eigenmode ordering, linear coordinate decoding is truncated Fourier reconstruction with normalized squared error scaling as r^(-1/D).
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4 bounds epsilon squared by a finite-lattice expression proportional to ((r/Vol_D)^(1/D)-sqrt(D)/2)^(-1); asymptotically this is r^(-1/D), giving r^-1 for a one-dimensional continuum and r^-1/2 for two dimensions. The proof projects lattice coordinates onto the top-r Fourier basis, evaluates the omitted tail, and bounds the number of reciprocal-lattice sites.

anchors.section: E.5 error and lattice-count bounds / Equations 119-129

key_findings.claim: Author-reported probing result: projected year embeddings show the predicted low-rank error decay and a double-descent peak near the 60-sample interpolation threshold.
key_findings.evidence: For years 1900-2020, Appendix A says 100 random trials use 60 training embeddings and 60 test embeddings; Figure 2 plots mean and standard deviation. The displayed test curve falls from roughly 0.3 at very low rank to about 0.05 around rank 10-20, rises above 1 near rank 60, then falls again. Values are approximate readings from a log-scale plot, not a supplied result table.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the cited Figure 2 implementation does not compute the MSE defined in Proposition 4, and its split size does not match Appendix A.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines epsilon squared as a ratio of squared Euclidean errors and labels Figure 2's y-axis MSE. In the cited repository at commit 64e3d97a637d4a6b49e92703ea89cb1a99b1e00e, fig2.ipynb instead stores std(y-yhat)/std(y), an unsquared normalized residual standard deviation. It selects 60 training indices from 121 inclusive years 1900-2020, leaving 61 tests, whereas Appendix A says the remaining 60 form the test set. The plotted 0.7*r^-1 reference line therefore does not constitute a direct numerical validation of the stated MSE theorem.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the empirical 'word embeddings trained on Wikipedia' are spectral constructions, not direct word2vec training runs in this paper.
key_findings.evidence: The main text repeatedly describes word embeddings trained on Wikipedia, but Appendix A.2 states that the authors construct M* and obtain W by diagonalizing it and evaluating Equation 2. The connection to gradient-trained word2vec is imported from prior work and depends on a quartic approximation and special balanced asymmetric factorization, so the experiments directly validate the spectral surrogate rather than optimization-to-geometry causation.

key_findings.claim: Author-stated theory-to-data qualification: real Wikipedia M* violates the simplified positive-semidefinite assumption and prevents correct absolute amplitude prediction.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B.3 reports a roughly symmetric empirical spectrum with rank(M+) approximately rank(M-). For asymmetric embeddings, the Gram matrix factors |M*|, not M*. The paper nonetheless estimates Figure 1-2 exponential kernels from the easier-to-compute M* block and explicitly says it typically misses absolute amplitude scale while appearing to recover relative amplitudes and wavenumbers.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported corpus-statistics result: month and year co-occurrences are approximately translation symmetric and fit exponential distance kernels, but important residuals remain.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 fits the month M* and |M*| curves with periodized exponential widths sigma=4.2 and 6.8, respectively, and shows one-standard-deviation variation across months. The main diagonal is a visible exception. Figure 6 fits shifted open-boundary year kernels with widths 125 for M*, 120 for |M*|, 115 for M+, and 90 for M-; the M- long-range tail departs strongly from the exponential curve. No likelihood, R-squared, held-out fit, or alternative-kernel comparison is reported.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the diagonal-mismatch dismissal in Figure 5 is valid only for a constant diagonal residual, which the paper does not establish.
key_findings.evidence: The caption argues that the main-diagonal discrepancy cannot affect eigenvector ordering because adding kappa I shifts every eigenvalue equally. That conclusion holds if the empirical-minus-kernel diagonal is the same kappa for every month. The displayed month-specific diagonals and error bars are not shown to satisfy that condition; a nonconstant diagonal perturbation can rotate eigenvectors and alter gaps.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer assessment: the geography comparison is qualitative and contains post-hoc fitting and component selection.
key_findings.evidence: For 48 contiguous states, the theory uses M*ij=10 exp(-dij/20), with both parameters chosen by visual inspection. Figure 3 compares slow spatial modes with d=1000 and d=25000 spectral word embeddings, 768-dimensional EmbeddingGemma, and Gemma 2 2B layer-6 activations. The first Gemma eigenmode is omitted because it tracks multi-token state names, color scales are independently chosen, and no alignment or goodness-of-fit score is reported.

anchors.section: Figure 3 and 3.1 Beyond the lattice approximation

key_findings.claim: Author-reported robustness result: a month circle can reappear at dimension 1000 after every direct month-month M* entry is set to zero.
key_findings.evidence: With vocabulary V=25,000 and embedding dimension d=1000, Figure 4 shows a correctly ordered circular month embedding and a reconstructed month Gram matrix despite setting the 12x12 target block M*S to zero. May is excluded from the left-panel PCA. The latent-variable argument attributes recovery to many seasonal helper words whose collective modes have eigenvalues and eigengaps growing with vocabulary size.

key_findings.claim: Contradiction audit: the abstract's corpus-removal description does not match the actual robustness intervention.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract describes perturbation by removing sentences in which two months co-occur. Appendix A.1.4 instead sets Pij=PiPj for target month pairs, equivalently forcing only the M* month-month block to zero after corpus statistics have been computed. This preserves unigram counts and all month-helper statistics and is not equivalent to deleting sentences and recomputing the full corpus distribution.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer assessment: the helper-word reconstruction is target-informed and therefore not an independent discovery of seasonality.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix C.1 defines each vocabulary word's seasonality score from its affinity to the existing month embeddings, then selects the top 100 words and uses those words to reconstruct the month geometry. Seasonal helpers outperform random helpers and 17 number words fail, but the selection criterion already uses the target representation. The claimed approximately 1/sqrt(H) error scaling is a plotted guide without a fitted exponent or selection-held-out test.

key_findings.claim: Author-reported negative cases identify where translation symmetry visibly breaks.
key_findings.evidence: Static May is displaced by modal-verb polysemy until excluded from PCA; historical word embeddings show local kinks around World Wars I and II; Gemma 2's digit tokenization creates bright off-diagonal year similarities; and the empirical year M- kernel has a non-exponential long-range floor. Context resolves May in Gemma, but these cases show that distance is not the only organizing variable.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer assessment: cross-architecture evidence is consistent with the hypothesis but does not establish that pair statistics causally drive LLM geometry.
key_findings.evidence: The deep-model study uses one Gemma 2 2B checkpoint and one prompt template per category, plus one EmbeddingGemma model for states. It reports visual PCA agreement but no corpus intervention followed by LLM retraining, causal activation test, alternative statistic control, representational-similarity score, prompt distribution, model-family sweep, or held-out concept set. The mechanism is proved only for the spectral word-embedding surrogate.

key_findings.claim: Author extension: continuous seasonality and independent binary attributes occupy orthogonal spectral subspaces in a combined generative model.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix D assigns every word a seasonal phase and d binary attributes, factorizes their co-occurrence influences, and decomposes the exact PMI into Kronecker terms. Theorem 5 yields Fourier seasonal modes and Walsh singleton attribute modes with separate nonzero eigenvalues, showing that circular manifolds can coexist with linear analogy geometry under the model's independence assumptions.

anchors.section: D Combined Model / Equations 42-45 and E.1-E.2

key_findings.claim: Reviewer assessment: the robustness theorem is asymptotic and does not certify the finite Wikipedia intervention.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.1 argues that at fixed embedding dimension and N tending to infinity, seasonal eigenvalues and eigengaps scale with N while a fixed 12x12 perturbation remains small, invoking Weyl or Davis-Kahan. It does not give the finite-N perturbation norm, measured eigengap, angular bound, or competition from other latent variables for V=25,000 and d=1000; the result explains a possible mechanism but does not quantitatively predict Figure 4.

techniques.role: Uses bounded normalized excess co-occurrence M* as a third-order approximation to PMI and the spectral target for word embeddings.
Constructs embeddings from eigenvectors and absolute eigenvalues of M* rather than optimizing word2vec in the reported experiments.
Models pair statistics as a function only of distance on a latent temporal or spatial continuum.
Derives exact sine/cosine representation coordinates for periodic semantic lattices.
Derives noninteger historical-time modes by treating the exponential kernel as a Green's function with centered boundary conditions.
Tests the predicted Fourier-tail scaling and double descent when decoding numeric year from top PCA modes.
Sets all month-month M* entries to zero to test whether the remaining vocabulary reconstructs circular order.
Explains collective robust eigenmodes through many words modulated by a shared periodic latent variable.
Ranks words by month affinity and measures how seasonal versus random helpers reconstruct the month Gram matrix.
Compares analytic modes to prompted Gemma 2 2B residual activations across layers.

evaluations.setting: November 2023 English Wikipedia, 3.37M articles after filtering, 2.72B tokens, V=25,000, weighted symmetric context window L=16
evaluations.metric: Month normalized co-occurrence versus circular month difference and exponential-kernel width
evaluations.result: Figure 5 fits the M* curve with sigma=4.2 and the |M*| curve with sigma=6.8; off-diagonal means follow the periodized exponential visually, while the zero-difference diagonal is a systematic exception.
evaluations.baseline: A distance-only periodized exponential kernel; no alternative kernel or held-out goodness-of-fit baseline is reported.

evaluations.setting: English-Wikipedia historical years approximately 1700-2020 under the same M* construction
evaluations.metric: Year normalized co-occurrence versus absolute year difference and shifted exponential-kernel width
evaluations.result: Figure 6 reports fitted widths 125 for M*, 120 for |M*|, 115 for M+, and 90 for M-. The M- curve retains a substantial long-range floor that the exponential model misses.
evaluations.baseline: A shifted open-boundary exponential kernel; no scored competing kernel is evaluated.

evaluations.setting: Linear decoding of inclusive years 1900-2020 from rank-r Wikipedia spectral embeddings over 100 random splits
evaluations.metric: Paper-labeled normalized MSE with trial mean and standard deviation
evaluations.result: The plotted test curve is approximately 0.3 at very low rank, about 0.05 near rank 10-20, above 1 near the r=60 interpolation threshold, and about 0.15 by rank 100. The cited code actually computes normalized residual standard deviation, not MSE, and uses 61 rather than 60 held-out years.
evaluations.baseline: A visual 0.7*r^-1 reference line plus training error; Figure 13 adds optimally regularized probing to remove the double-descent peak.

evaluations.setting: Calendar-month direct-statistics ablation on V=25,000 Wikipedia vocabulary with d=1000 spectral embeddings
evaluations.metric: PCA ordering and reconstructed centered Gram matrix after setting the 12x12 month block M*S to zero
evaluations.result: The 11-month PCA excluding May remains circular and ordered, and its Gram matrix visually resembles the original month block despite d being only 4% of V.
evaluations.baseline: The unablated month co-occurrence geometry; no Procrustes or matrix-error number is supplied for Figure 4.

evaluations.setting: Month reconstruction from auxiliary words with all direct month-month entries zeroed
evaluations.metric: Procrustes embedding error versus helper count H
evaluations.result: Top-100 month-affinity-selected seasonal words reduce the plotted error from roughly 0.65 at a few helpers to about 0.2 near H=100 and recover correct ordering; random words remain near 0.5 even near H=1000, while 17 number words produce no clear month order. Values are approximate plot readings.
evaluations.baseline: Random vocabulary helpers and nonseasonal number-word helpers.

evaluations.setting: Forty-eight contiguous US states across a theoretical kernel, d=1000 and d=25,000 spectral word embeddings, 768D EmbeddingGemma, and Gemma 2 2B layer-6 activations
evaluations.metric: Visual correspondence of the top three geographic PCA modes
evaluations.result: All displayed models show broad east-west, north-south, or regional slow variation qualitatively. The Gemma first mode is omitted as tokenization-dominated, each color scale is separately optimized, and no numerical alignment score is given.
evaluations.baseline: Numerically diagonalized M*ij=10*exp(-dij/20), with parameters selected by visual inspection.

evaluations.setting: Calendar-date vocabulary in which 365 date phrases are tokenized as individual words
evaluations.metric: Two-dimensional PCA projections across component pairs
evaluations.result: Figure 9 shows Lissajous curves for the 365 dates with qualitative frequency and amplitude agreement to Corollary 2; no fit statistic is reported.

evaluations.setting: Contextual disambiguation of the polysemous token May across Gemma 2 2B layers 0-25
evaluations.metric: Deviation of month representations from circular PCA geometry
evaluations.result: With single-token month prompts, May remains distorted through the network; with 'The month of the year is x', its distortion visually fades across layers.

limitations: Author-stated: the theory is derived for word-embedding algorithms; contextual LLMs can disambiguate and transform representations in ways the theory does not explain.
Author-stated: the work treats semantic relations characterized by continuous attributes; hierarchical and other geometric structures remain unexplained.
Author-stated: real M* is not positive semidefinite, so fitting M* instead of the matrix absolute value generally misses absolute mode amplitudes.
Author-stated: the 2D geography result is only expected to be qualitatively correct because states are not a uniform lattice and the matrix is diagonalized numerically.
Author-stated: May polysemy, historical wars, and digit tokenization visibly perturb the ideal manifolds.
Reviewer-identified: the paper's Figure 2 implementation computes an unsquared normalized residual standard deviation while the figure and Proposition 4 call the quantity MSE.
Reviewer-identified: the inclusive 1900-2020 pool contains 121 years, so selecting 60 training items leaves 61 tests, contradicting Appendix A's statement that 60 remain.
Reviewer-identified: the empirical word embeddings are constructed by spectral factorization rather than trained with word2vec in this work.
Reviewer-identified: the abstract describes deleting co-occurring-month sentences, but the implemented intervention only resets target-pair probabilities after corpus statistics are computed.
Reviewer-identified: no quantitative curve-fit, representational-similarity, manifold, or cross-model alignment metric supports the main visual comparisons.
Reviewer-identified: the geography kernel scale and amplitude are selected visually, May is excluded from static PCA, and a Gemma component is omitted because it tracks token count.
Reviewer-identified: independently normalized color maps make qualitative spatial-mode agreement easier to perceive and harder to falsify.
Reviewer-identified: one English corpus, one decoder LLM, one text-embedding model, one prompt template per category, and three hand-selected semantic domains limit generality.
Reviewer-identified: no LLM is retrained after changing corpus symmetry, so the claimed causal direction from pair statistics to LLM geometry remains an inference.

Reviewer-identified: higher-order token statistics, shared training objectives, entity semantics, and architecture can generate correlated geometry without the proposed pairwise mechanism being sufficient.
Reviewer-identified: the d>=rank(M*) and monotone-eigenspectrum assumptions needed for exact results do not describe the moderate-rank real-model regime directly.
Reviewer-identified: the finite-data robustness experiment is not accompanied by the eigengap and perturbation-norm quantities required for a Davis-Kahan bound.
Reviewer-identified: top seasonal helpers are selected using affinity to the target month embeddings, creating target-informed selection in the reconstruction demonstration.
Reviewer-identified: the displayed 1/sqrt(H) helper-error trend is not supported by a fitted exponent, confidence interval, or held-out helper-selection procedure.
Reviewer-identified: the diagonal-kernel residual is dismissed using a kappa-I argument without showing that the month-specific diagonal residual is constant.

Reviewer-identified: coordinate probing demonstrates accessibility, not that the model uses these coordinates in computation; unlike prior intervention studies, this paper supplies no causal LLM behavior test.
Reviewer-identified: code randomness is not seeded in the displayed probing loop, and reproducibility depends on large precomputed co-occurrence artifacts not distributed in the small repository.
failure_modes: Polysemous words combine unrelated senses and leave the ideal latent manifold.
Tokenizer boundaries dominate principal components, especially for multi-token place names and digit-wise years.
Historical shocks such as wars break temporal stationarity and create local kinks in year manifolds.
Nonuniform item density and open boundaries distort plane-wave eigenmodes near the edges of a continuum.
A distance-only kernel confounds shared latent position with topical, political, cultural, or lexical similarity.
The empirical M* matrix has large negative spectrum, so a PSD-only argument predicts the wrong Gram matrix or amplitude scale.
PCA truncation splits or reorders nearly degenerate modes when empirical eigenvalues are not monotone in wavenumber.
Pairwise symmetry appears in a corpus but higher-order context causes an LLM to encode a different geometry.
The same visual manifold arises from token morphology, prompt construction, or architecture rather than training-data co-occurrence.
Post-hoc removal of components or items turns a nonmatching representation into an apparently matching projection.
A constant shift removes the mean mode, but a nonconstant diagonal or heteroskedastic perturbation rotates the semantic eigenspace.
Helper words selected through target affinity reconstruct the target even when no independently defined seasonal variable generalizes.
A fixed-size perturbation is negligible asymptotically but large relative to a small finite eigengap.
Linear probe error improves because PCA and labels share ordering, without the language model using the representation for behavior.
Cyclic or spatial geometry changes across languages, corpora, prompts, layers, checkpoints, or tokenizers.
The spectral surrogate matches a final embedding even though actual gradient training learns different intermediate geometry or local minima.
reusable_insights: Before interpreting a representation manifold, measure whether the corresponding data statistics possess the same symmetry group.
Translation-invariant kernels provide a direct route from pair statistics to Fourier eigenmodes, including amplitude predictions from the kernel spectrum.
Handle open boundaries explicitly: centering changes even modes and can produce noninteger wavenumbers rather than simple Fourier series.
Linear coordinate decoding from a low-pass Fourier code is truncated series reconstruction; its error is governed by the missing high-frequency tail.
Distinguish a true trained embedding from a spectral surrogate, even when prior work argues they are close.
When a target geometry survives direct-pair ablation, look for many auxiliary variables carrying the same latent factor and quantify the eigengap that makes the code robust.
Use negative helpers and random helpers, but select positive helpers independently of the target representation to avoid circular reconstruction evidence.
Report fit scores, subspace angles, Procrustes errors, and held-out predictions in addition to visually aligned PCA panels.
Pre-register component exclusions and common color scales; token-count and polysemy confounds should be evaluated, not removed only after inspection.
A correlation-to-geometry mechanism becomes substantially stronger when the training distribution is manipulated and a newly trained model follows the predicted geometric change.
Metric code should implement exactly the theorem's squared or unsquared quantity, and sample counts should be checked against inclusive ranges.
Separate representational accessibility from causal use by combining probes with interventions on the identified manifold.
open_questions: Does actual word2vec training on the same corpus recover the predicted amplitudes, wavenumbers, and ablation behavior as closely as direct M* factorization?
If calendar co-occurrence symmetry is selectively changed in a training corpus and a transformer is retrained, does its month manifold change according to the new kernel spectrum?
How much variance in LLM subspaces is explained by pairwise M* after controlling for tokenization, morphology, prompts, and higher-order context?
Do the predictions replicate across model families, sizes, checkpoints, languages, tokenizers, layers, and naturally occurring prompt distributions?
Which quantitative metric best distinguishes true Fourier correspondence from visually similar PCA projections?
Can the full non-PSD |M*| kernel be estimated efficiently enough to make correct absolute-amplitude predictions on large vocabularies?
Are empirical eigenvalues sufficiently monotone with wavenumber for Proposition 4, and how does mode reordering change the decoding rate?
What is the correct empirical decoding curve after computing the normalized squared error defined in Equation 10 and using an unambiguous 60/61 split?
Can a finite-N Davis-Kahan calculation using the measured Wikipedia perturbation norm and eigengaps predict the d=1000 robustness result quantitatively?
Do helpers selected from external seasonal metadata, without access to month embeddings, reproduce the 1/sqrt(H) curve?
Can an alternative non-exponential or anisotropic kernel explain the month diagonal and historical M- tail better out of sample?
How should the theory handle multiple interacting continuous variables, nonuniform latent densities, polysemy, and context-dependent coordinates?
Does the LLM causally use the predicted high-frequency overtones for temporal arithmetic, spatial reasoning, or historical ordering?
Can symmetry-based statistics predict manifolds for color, temperature, age, hierarchy, or toroidal multi-factor concepts before inspecting representations?
When does low-dimensional truncation improve semantic robustness, and when does it erase task-relevant local variation?
Can common, pre-registered subspace alignment and color scaling eliminate the need to omit May or tokenization-dominated components?

competitive_landscape.title: Closed-Form Training Dynamics Reveal Learned Features and Linear Structure in Word2Vec-like Models
competitive_landscape.difference: This prior same-author work derives the quartic word2vec surrogate and closed-form spectral training dynamics that the target paper takes as its bridge from corpus statistics to W. The target extends that machinery from generic eigenspaces and analogies to continuous translation symmetry, Fourier manifolds, coordinate decoding, and seasonal robustness, but its empirical embeddings remain constructions of the antecedent surrogate.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Emergence of Linear Analogies in Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Korchinski et al. use binary semantic attributes and co-occurrence interactions to explain parallelogram analogies and robustness after direct-pair removal. The target generalizes the same program to continuous periodic/open attributes, derives curved Fourier manifolds, and combines seasonality with binary Walsh modes in Appendix D.

competitive_landscape.title: Not All Language Model Features Are One-Dimensionally Linear
competitive_landscape.difference: Engels et al. automatically discover circular month/day features with sparse autoencoders and use activation interventions to show causal involvement in modular arithmetic. The target explains why such circles can arise from language statistics and predicts their harmonics, but does not match the competitor's automated discovery or causal behavioral tests.

competitive_landscape.title: The Origins of Representation Manifolds in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Modell et al. explain representation manifolds through intrinsic feature geometry and shortest on-manifold paths reflected by cosine similarity, validating predictions on text embeddings and LLM activations. The target instead derives extrinsic PCA coordinates from translation symmetry in pair co-occurrence kernels, providing explicit Fourier frequencies and amplitudes but under narrower spectral assumptions.

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Represent Space and Time
competitive_landscape.difference: Gurnee and Tegmark establish robust spatial and temporal linear probes across six datasets, Llama-2 and Pythia sizes, layers, entity types, and prompt variants. The target provides a Fourier mechanism and rank-dependent decoding bound, but its deep-model empirical scope is much narrower and does not re-establish the broad robustness controls.

competitive_landscape.title: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Prieto et al. train controlled bag-of-words superposition models and show that correlated features generate semantic clusters and cycles through constructive interference, including effects of weight decay. The target analyzes spectral word embeddings and natural-language symmetries to derive exact Fourier manifolds; the competitor offers an explicit trained-network intervention but a different encoding objective and binary bag-of-words setting.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Sequence Models Tend to Memorize Geometrically; It Is Unclear Why
competitive_landscape.difference: Noroozizadeh et al. show transformer and graph-memory geometry emerging from local associations and connect it to Node2Vec spectral bias, including non-co-occurring entities. The target specializes spectral emergence to natural-language continuous variables and supplies closed-form Fourier geometry and a collective latent-variable mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers Learn Factored Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Shai et al. contrast product-space and orthogonal factored representations in transformers trained on synthetic processes with known latent structure and identify a conditional-independence trade-off. The target studies continuous natural-language factors through pair statistics and Fourier modes; its Appendix D also predicts orthogonal seasonal and binary subspaces but without transformer training controls on the combined generative model.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A single organizing principle—translation symmetry in low-order language co-occurrence statistics—unifies circular cyclic concepts, rippled continuous sequences, spatial manifolds, linear coordinate decoding, and robustness to removal of direct target-pair evidence; the paper analytically predicts full manifold geometry and its collective origin.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The work derives exact periodic Fourier modes, open-boundary exponential-kernel modes, a rank-dependent coordinate-decoding bound, a continuous seasonal latent-variable model, and an orthogonal continuous-plus-binary spectrum. It compares predictions with a 2.72B-token Wikipedia spectral construction, Gemma 2 2B, EmbeddingGemma, month/year kernel measurements, target-block ablations, helper reconstructions, and 48-state spatial modes.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the unusually explicit bridge from a measured symmetry to frequencies, amplitudes, boundary-dependent curves, and decoding-rate predictions, together with a plausible large-vocabulary robustness mechanism. The boundary is narrower than the causal language suggests: the word vectors are spectral surrogates, real M* violates the simplified assumptions, key LLM panels are visual and post-processed, the robustness intervention is not corpus sentence removal, and the probing code does not implement the stated MSE. Prior work already discovered and causally validated circles, decoded space/time, derived word2vec spectral dynamics, and explained binary analogy robustness; this paper's real contribution is their continuous-symmetry synthesis and analytic specialization, not the first observation of the geometries or proof that pair statistics cause them in LLMs.

reviewer_notes: The complete 36-page ICML/PMLR artifact corresponding to current arXiv v3 was read end to end, including references, experimental Appendix A, word-embedding review B, all additional figures and helper analysis C, combined latent model D, and every proof step in E.1-E.5. The reading is pinned to the exact local PDF/text hashes above, and pages containing dense figures were inspected from the PDF. I also audited the paper-cited public repository at commit 64e3d97a637d4a6b49e92703ea89cb1a99b1e00e; the Figure 2 metric and 60/61 split discrepancies are therefore marked explicitly rather than inferred from the plot. Eight exact-version primary competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. Confidence is high in the theorem statements, artifact-level contradictions, and experimental scope audit; it is intentionally lower than certainty on whether all long mathematical derivations are error-free because this was a full reading and consistency audit, not machine-checked formal verification.
